newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Two dead, 60 wounded in attack on Tajik president.
newsitem.headline: Two dead, 60 wounded in attack on Tajik president.

text.p: Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov survived an assassination attempt on Wednesday which killed two people and injured 60, his spokesman said.
Rakhmonov, 45, had a grenade thrown at his feet while getting out of a car during a visit to the northern town of Khudjand.
The president was hurt in the legs but was able to limp down the steps from his aircraft on returning to the capital, Dushanbe.
Rakhmonov spoke briefly to officials, who met him on the tarmac, before being rushed away amid heavy security.
"The president's health is not endangered," presidential spokesman Zafar Saidov said.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin issued a statement voicing his "anger and indignation" at the attack and wished Rakhmonov a quick recovery. Russia stations thousands of troops in the Central Asian state to guard its borders and carry out peacekeeping tasks.
Saidov said the attack took place at 10.30 a.m. (0530 GMT) in Khudjand, capital of the Leninabad region. The dead were both men, a 17-year-old student and a 30-year-old teacher.
"The president, after being treated for his wounds, said the attack was the hand of a terrorist group and a provocative act," Saidov said.

He said 21-year-old Firdavs Dustboboyev, who he said had organised an anti-government protest in the town in May last year, was responsible for the attack and was arrested almost immediately afterwards.

Tajikistan, a former Soviet republic, is still reeling from a four-year civil war in which tens of thousands of people were killed. Armed groups still roam the mountain state, which borders Afghanistan and China.
A spokesman for Tajikistan's armed Islamic opposition, Rakhmonov's main foe in the civil war, told Reuters the group had no connection with the attack.

"We categorically deny any connection with the attack by the United Tajik Opposition," said Abdunabi Sattorzoda, a member of an opposition delegation in Dushanbe which has been involved in now stalled peace talks with the government.

Sattorzoda and diplomatic sources in Dushanbe said the attack could be linked to unrest over a prison riot in Khudzhand earlier this month, led by prisoners involved in last year's anti-government demonstration.
Tajik security forces killed around 20 prisoners when they stormed the jail.

The violence is unusual for the northern Leninabad region, separated from the rest of the country by a chain of spectacular mountains. It has been spared much of the bloody conflict which has raged elsewhere.
